parameters.query:
WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO idempotency_keys (key) VALUES ('{{ $json.dedupeKey }}')
  ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING id
),
logged AS (
  INSERT INTO transactions (correlation_id, doc_type, direction, partner, stream, status, external_ids, payload_ref)
  SELECT '{{ $json.correlationId }}', '{{ $json.docType }}', '{{ $json.direction }}', 'DCG', 'TEST', '{{ $json.status }}', '{{ $json.externalIds }}'::jsonb, '{{ $json.fileName }}'
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ins)
  RETURNING id
)
SELECT
  '{{ $json.correlationId }}' AS correlation_id,
  (SELECT id FROM ins) IS NOT NULL AS is_new,
  (SELECT id FROM logged) AS transaction_id;

meta.instructions: Pulls the FULL ApparelMagic item catalog and pushes it to DCG as one 888. `Get All AM Products` and `Get All AM Inventory` are HTTP nodes using the Query Auth credential with n8n built-in CURSOR pagination: AM caps pages at 100, ignores page_number, and paginates by meta.pagination.last_id (sent back via pagination[last_id]; empty on page 1). AM auth time expires in minutes, but n8n re-evaluates the time query expression on every paginated request so it stays fresh. Stops when a page returns <100 rows; 2000-page (200k) safety cap. Combine & Parse Items flattens all pages ($(...).all().flatMap(i=>i.json.response)) and merges products (header: division_id, unit_of_measure, package_config, att1_customer) + inventory (per-SKU UPC/color/size) into canonical Items; Build 888 X12 emits one G39 per SKU with the four Aaron-mapped fields (G3917 package_config, G3919 unit_of_measure, G3923 division_id, G3924 att1_customer). One batched file for the whole catalog (~1,536 products / ~15,080 SKUs now, heading toward ~100k). SCALE CAVEAT: at ~100k this is 1,000+ sequential paginated calls + a large in-memory dataset/file -> run on self-hosted/high-memory n8n, schedule overnight/weekly, and consider chunking into multiple 888s (e.g. per division) if DCG accepts. After import re-select credentials: Query Auth account (both Get All nodes), Postgres account (Claim & Log, Mark Sent), AWS account (Upload to S3, StartFileTransfer). Uses usageIndicator T / stream TEST. INLINE DELIVERY VERIFICATION: after StartFileTransfer, Wait 5s -> ListFileTransferResults -> Verify Transfer (DCG) confirms the file actually reached DCG (StartFileTransfer 200 only means AWS accepted the request). If the transfer FAILED (or no result yet), Verify throws -> execution fails -> the SCL: Error Alerts error workflow emails help@goodmove.xyz. Only a COMPLETED transfer proceeds to Mark Sent. Set this flow Settings -> Error Workflow = SCL: Error Alerts. Re-select the AWS account credential on ListFileTransferResults after import.
